author: P00000L5
quote:
When reading this review and any others with a low score, ask yourself: am I going to dismiss this review with a score of 1 from a random user but believe the many perfect scores of 100, something just unprecedented and seemingly impossible.

 This game is not perfect, and I’ve rated it as such (maybe a little more graciously).  Many have been disappointed, me included, in how it decided to drive forward the GTA franchise. But the critic review has disappointed us the most. Universally, we can all agree this is not an 100 greatest game of all time. 

The performance is not the best, often with many bugs and glitches, just search online for compilations of this. FPS falls to low 20s and even below. Now this would normally bring down a reviewers score on any other game, this time 160 critics seemingly decided to look past that and still give this a glowing 100 perfect score. 

The story has been described as many as boring, which I can completely agree with for the first 20 hours or so. Instead of the normal GTA heist and action packed gameplay we are all used to, we get to instead do chores, play life, and take care of a woman who seemingly cannot think her decisions through. Lucia constantly makes bad decisions and for some reason seemingly forgets she has a child after being released from jail. The story just seems to drag on and splits off into many confusing directions and leaves me wondering, what happened to GTA. Certain characters are barred off from being attacked or certain locations are off limits. Classic GTA gameplay has been swapped out, for what can only be described as a sanitization of the freedom we all loved.  

The one thing that can be unanimously agreed upon is the graphics. It is a very gorgeous at times breathtaking games but at what cost? A game that cannot break 30 FPS in 2026, that has many bugs and glitches, that lacks a story that draws us in. At what point do we stop caring about graphics and start caring about what matters: FUN. All of these problems can be seen as a direct result of all the money and effort being poured into graphics that nobody asked for. Now this is not the first time this has happened though. Most modern triple a games have been following this trend and it’s disappointing. Are we as players going to collectively continue to support this and watch as our favorite franchises are torn apart and our favorite developers are fired? How is it that games with a quarter of the budget and capture all of us but the games with the big corporation backing cannot?

We play games to have fun. We don’t play games to play life.
